decisions.reason: The spec named a capability the module does not yet provide. It now lists the declaration and spec changes the plan makes, and says how code-work reaches the capability through the provides option.

The contract text lists installer writes only, but groundwork and mempalace already put run-time files in the untracked local area. The spec now states that practice, cites it, and says nothing is declared or upgraded there.
The scan was vague and could not be tested. It now covers every field, reuses the notes helper rule list, refuses without echoing the matched text, and names the tests.
The plan-close capture was undefined. The spec now says which plan sections are read, when it runs, how duplicates and failures are handled, and how the clause is conditioned on the capability.

Source and step had no bounds and the total size was unbounded. Every header value is now one line with a limit, the whole item has a limit, and unreadable files are listed without being printed. The acceptance list tests these.

Applied in a lighter form than suggested. Creation is exclusive with a numeric suffix, writes go through a temporary name and a rename, and the log line is one short append. I took no lock because a double-added title is harmless and the owner can drop one.

Items written by hand or by an older version could print a credential to the conversation. The same scan now runs before show, drop or list prints a field, and the output names the field and rule without the text.
